overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that extreme cosmic scenarios, counter-intuitive space facts, and 'What If' hypothetical environmental drops drive the highest velocity and engagement (e.g., Venus, liquid diamond planets, and extreme exoplanets like TrES-2b and planetary-scale extreme phenomena). Videos published within the last 7 days exhibit significantly higher views-per-day and like ratios compared to older legacy uploads, indicating strong algorithmic favorability toward heightened curiosity loops and sensory-driven hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) generated massive engagement shortly after release compared to generic science facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, immersive hypothetical planetary survival/immersion hooks ('What If You Fell Into...').

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Cosmic Realities & Extreme Exoplanet Physics
winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views), 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (723 views), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,027 views) show exceptional traction.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form concepts featuring bizarre, counter-intuitive celestial physics and extreme exoplanetary weather.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and generic brain hacks underperformed significantly, showing poor viewer conversion.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize abstract psychological micro-facts unless framed through an urgent, high-stakes cinematic mystery hook.

weak_patterns.pattern: Rehashed Animal Facts Without Exotic Context
weak_patterns.evidence: Standard animal trivia like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (varying low-to-moderate velocity on older reruns) show lower relative daily momentum than space content.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal or biology topics toward extreme cinematic survival or prehistoric/deep-sea horror micro-narratives.

next_video.concept: Stepping onto a rogue planet drifting through interstellar space with absolute zero thermal energy
next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-action with an audio-visual warning of instant atmospheric freezing upon stepping onto a rogue world lit only by distant quasars.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite having no sun, the planet's core is sustained by nuclear friction, creating subterranean oceans of liquid nitrogen.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' and extreme cosmic temperature hooks while introducing a completely fresh celestial phenomenon not present in past uploads.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamond planets, raining glass, or Venus
Avoid reusing space silence, star age, or brain/memory themes
Ensure all physical phenomena cited are scientifically accurate

experiment: Test a 15-second high-pacing rogue planet 'What If' scenario against a 21-second narrative structure to determine optimal audience retention for extreme space concepts.
